scenes.name: the van, the courier, and a server
scenes.visual: Frame 1920 x 1080; keep x < 420, y < 110 clear for the chapter label. A calm stage with no computers until b4. Lower-middle band, y 640 to 780: a road drawn left to right from x 300 to x 1640, with an upper lane (courier) and a lower lane (van). Left end: a post-office icon (a small building with a mailbox). Right end: three small house icons. Neither end carries a text label; the icons say it. Letters are small blue envelope icons. Top band, y 150 to 330: two definition cards side by side with neutral white outlines, because this scene is about neither compute nor bytes. Left card: stopwatch icon, title 'Latency'. Right card: stacked-envelopes icon, title 'Throughput'. Each card shows one short line only while it is being defined ('time for one letter', 'letters per day'), then keeps its title and icon alone. Each vehicle gets a one-line ledger at the right end of its lane, white, 28 px. A grey 'illustrative' tag sits bottom-right from b2 until the morph in b4. From b3 a slider sits centred under the road, labelled 'wait before leaving', with a motorbike icon at its left end and a van icon at its right end; it stays to the end of the scene and is reused for the server. In b4 one continuous morph re-dresses the same stage for a server. Never more than five text items on screen besides numbers. The idea the motion makes visible: one service, two different questions, and a single dial that trades one for the other.

beats.say: Take the post. Latency: how long one letter takes to arrive. Throughput: how many letters arrive per day.
beats.show: On 'Take the post', the road draws on from left to right and the post office and houses pop in at its ends. On 'Latency', the left card drops into the top band with its line 'time for one letter'; one blue envelope travels from the post office to the houses while the card's stopwatch runs, stopping as the envelope lands. On 'Throughput', the right card drops in with 'letters per day'; a steady stream of envelopes flows along the road and a counter on the card ticks upward. As the beat ends both description lines fade, leaving titles and icons.

beats.say: A weekly van, crammed full, has enormous throughput and terrible latency. A motorbike courier with one letter is the reverse.
beats.show: The stream stops. On 'A weekly van', a van icon parks on the lower lane at the post office with a small grey tag 'once a week' above it; on 'crammed full', envelopes pour in and a counter on its side runs to '7,000'. On 'enormous throughput', the 'once a week' tag fades, the van drives to the houses and its ledger lands at the lane's right end: '≈ 1,000/day · up to a week'. On 'terrible latency', one envelope drops into the empty post office and waits, glowing, while a ring of seven segments around it fills one segment per day. On 'motorbike courier', a motorbike icon on the upper lane carries one envelope to the houses in about a second, returns and repeats; its ledger lands: '≈ 20/day · under an hour'. The grey 'illustrative' tag fades in bottom-right.

beats.say: Neither is better. Unlike memory's latency and bandwidth, these pull against each other, through one choice: how long to wait before leaving.
beats.show: On 'Neither is better', a balance-scale icon between the two ledgers settles level, a grey tag 'different questions' beneath it. On 'Unlike memory's latency and bandwidth', that tag fades, both ledgers dim to 30% and a small grey inset fades in top-right: the container ship and motorbike courier from the earlier memory chapter, tagged 'independent'. On 'pull against each other', the inset and the ledgers fade out and a thin double-headed arrow pulls taut between the 'Latency' and 'Throughput' cards. On 'one choice', the slider draws on under the road. On 'how long to wait', its knob slides right: the van fills while the waiting letter's ring keeps filling, and a bar on the Throughput card grows; then the knob slides back left: the motorbike leaves at once with one envelope, the Latency card's stopwatch hand shortens and the Throughput bar shrinks.

beats.say: Not a computing idea, yet a serving system faces exactly this choice: wait to gather requests and do more, or answer at once and do less.
beats.show: On 'Not a computing idea', the 'illustrative' tag fades. On 'a serving system', one continuous morph: the post office becomes a G P U package icon, the houses a row of user icons, the envelopes blue request pills, the van a tray on the lower lane and the motorbike a single pill on the upper lane; the cards and slider stay. On 'wait to gather requests', the knob slides right: ten pills collect in the tray and leave together, and a counter at the lower lane's right end runs to '≈ 240 tokens/s'. On 'answer at once', the knob slides left: pills leave one by one on the upper lane and its counter reads '≈ 24 tokens/s'; on 'do less' that counter pulses once. A small grey tag under the counters: 'H100, weights only'.

beats.say: But the first request waits for the rest. That is why this chapter ends counting only tokens that arrive in time.
beats.show: On 'the first request', the knob slides right again; the leftmost pill in the tray pulses and a small stopwatch beside it runs while the other nine trickle in. On 'arrive in time', a small teal clock badge flickers once over each user icon, then fades: a promise of the chapter's last number. Final hold: the two cards in the top band, the slider, the G P U and the users.

scenes.name: two waits, and the phase behind each
scenes.visual: Keep x < 420, y < 110 clear. Opening layout: top half, a wide chat window centred (x 480 to 1440, y 130 to 420), its prompt bubble already sent and an empty reply area with a blinking cursor. Centre band, y 540: a horizontal time axis from x 240 to x 1700, schematic, with a small 'send' marker at its left end. On it, the shape of every streamed answer: an outlined pause bar from 'send' to the first token, then nine evenly spaced blue token pills. The pause bar fills amber, because it turns out to be arithmetic; the gaps between pills are marked coral, because they turn out to be bytes. From b2 the chat window fades, the timeline rises into the top band (y 200), and its labels stay at 28 px. The lower half then splits into two phase panels: left, amber outline, title 'prefill', an 80-layer stack of thin horizontal bars with a block of blue prompt pills beneath; right, coral outline, title 'decode', an identical stack with a single blue pill beneath. In b3 the panels shrink into two dots on a small roofline at bottom-centre, drawn as in the roofline chapter: both axes logarithmic, coral slanted ceiling, amber flat ceiling, white dashed ridge labelled '295'. At most five text items besides numbers at any moment; each beat says what leaves. The idea: one stream, two waits, and each wait made by one phase.

beats.say: Press send, and you feel two waits. The pause before the first word is time to first token. Each gap after it is time per output token.
beats.show: On 'Press send', a send-arrow icon flashes in the chat window and the 'send' marker drops onto the axis. On 'two waits', the outlined pause bar grows rightward from the marker while the cursor blinks, captioned 'a pause'. On 'the first word', the bar stops, the first blue pill lands and the reply shows 'The'. On 'time to first token', the bar fills amber from left to right, 'a pause' fades, and an amber bracket draws under it labelled 'time to first token' with 'TTFT' beneath. On 'Each gap after it', eight more pills land at even spacing, each adding a word to the reply. On 'time per output token', a coral bracket snaps into one gap, labelled 'time per output token' with 'TPOT, or inter-token latency' beneath and '≈ 42 ms on H100' at its end, then hops along two more gaps, the same width each time.

beats.say: Prefill makes the pause: the whole prompt passes through every layer before any output. Half a second for a short prompt, several seconds for a long one. Decode makes each gap: every token needs its own complete forward pass.
beats.show: On 'Prefill makes the pause', the chat window fades, the timeline rises into the top band, the 'send' label fades (its tick stays), and the long names shrink away, so the brackets keep only 'TTFT' and 'TPOT'. A connector draws from the TTFT bracket down to the left panel and its title 'prefill' lands. On 'the whole prompt passes through every layer', the block of prompt pills rises into the 80-layer stack all together, the layers lighting amber from bottom to top; on 'before any output', the block leaves the top of the stack and the first pill in the top band glows. On 'Half a second', the prompt block is short and a tag '≈ 0.5 s' pins to the pause bar; on 'several seconds', the block lengthens, the pause bar stretches with it and the tag changes to 'several s'. On 'Decode makes each gap', the tag fades, a connector draws from the TPOT bracket to the right panel and its title 'decode' lands. On 'its own complete forward pass', a single pill climbs the whole stack, the layers lighting coral; as it exits, the next pill lands in the top band and another single pill starts its climb.

beats.say: The pause decides whether a product feels responsive; the gaps, whether text reads comfortably or stutters and breaks concentration. Both are felt, and made at opposite ends of the roofline.
beats.show: The panel titles fade while the stacks keep their colours. On 'feels responsive', a short verdict 'feels responsive?' appears under TTFT; on 'reads comfortably', 'reads comfortably?' appears under TPOT. On 'stutters', the top-band pills jitter to uneven spacing; on 'breaks concentration', they settle back to even spacing. On 'Both are felt', the two verdicts fade. On 'opposite ends of the roofline', the two panels shrink into dots and fly onto the small roofline as it fades in at bottom-centre: the amber dot, labelled 'prefill', lands right of the dashed '295' ridge on the flat ceiling; the coral dot, labelled 'decode', lands far left on the slanted ceiling. Final hold text, white, under the roofline: 'opposite resource profiles'.

scenes.name: what a cache hit saves, and what it does not
scenes.visual: Keep x < 420, y < 110 clear. Two time lanes stacked across the centre, sharing one millisecond axis beneath them: 0 to 500 ms, drawn to scale at 3 px per ms (x 210 to 1710), ticks every 100 ms. Lane labels at the left, 28 px: top 'cold' beside a grey dashed empty-cache outline, bottom 'warm' beside a small teal cache badge. The weather-conversation bubble with its cloud-and-sun icon, as in the earlier cache chapters, sits top-centre during b1 only. Each lane first shows its prompt as a strip of 1,032 hairline cells spanning the axis, then collapses into a prefill block starting at 0, after which blue token pills land one every 42 ms (126 px apart). Top band, right half, built during the scene: a two-row verdict, 'Prefill: skipped for matched tokens' with a teal tick (b1) and 'Decode: identical, still reads all 140 GB' in coral (b3); in b4 the rows condense and gain the two waits. A small grey tag bottom-right throughout: 'idealised: H100 at full speed, no network or queue'. Colours as in the previous chapter: teal = keys and values already held, amber = prefill arithmetic, coral = bytes, blue = tokens. The idea: a hit moves the first token earlier and leaves the rhythm after it untouched.

beats.say: A cache hit skips prefill for every matched token. Warm, the weather conversation prefilled five tokens, not one thousand and thirty-two.
beats.show: The lanes, axis and lane labels draw on; the weather bubble settles top-centre. On 'skips prefill', the top-band row 'Prefill: skipped for matched tokens' lands with its teal tick. On 'Warm', the bottom lane's strip fills teal from the left for 1,027 cells and ends in 5 amber cells; a round magnifier callout pops up over the strip's right tip, showing the 5 amber cells enlarged with '5' beside them. On 'one thousand and thirty-two', the top lane's strip fills amber across every cell, with '1,032' at its right end.

beats.say: Two hundred and six times less work, yet only three and a half times less waiting: one read of the weights remains.
beats.show: The weather bubble, the magnifier and the strip numbers fade, and the top-band Prefill row dims to 30% for this beat. On 'Two hundred and six times less work', both strips collapse onto the axis, to scale: the cold one into an amber block from 0 to 148 ms (442 px), the warm one into a block from 0 to 42 ms (126 px); a first blue pill lands at each block's right end, with '≈ 148 ms' above the cold one and '≈ 42 ms' above the warm one, and a one-line tag lands at the left: '206× less work'. On 'three and a half times less waiting', the tag extends to '206× less work → 3.5× less wait' and a white bracket spans the two first pills, labelled '≈ 106 ms'. On 'one read of the weights', the warm block takes a coral outline, a hairline amber sliver inside it marks its arithmetic, and the label above its pill extends to '≈ 42 ms: one 140 GB read'.

beats.say: Decode is untouched, warm or cold: every token still reads all a hundred and forty gigabytes. Making one never depended on how the context was assembled.
beats.show: The ratio tag and the bracket fade, the warm block's label shortens to '≈ 42 ms', and the Prefill row returns to full strength. On 'Decode is untouched', blue pills land in both lanes one every 42 ms, 126 px apart, and a coral bracket of identical width marks one gap in each lane, each '≈ 42 ms'. The top-band row 'Decode: identical, still reads all 140 GB' lands in coral. On 'how the context was assembled', a slim bar slides out beside each lane label: the cold one freshly made, with an amber edge; the warm one teal with a 5-cell amber tip. Both morph into the same teal bar, labelled '1,032 tokens of keys and values'; the label fades after a second.

beats.say: So caching is purely a prefill optimisation: it shortens time to first token, never time per output token.
beats.show: On 'purely a prefill optimisation', the 'Prefill' row in the top band glows teal and both rows condense to their first words. On 'time to first token', amber brackets mark the pause in each lane, clearly different widths, and the Prefill row becomes 'Prefill skipped → TTFT shorter' with a teal down-arrow. On 'time per output token', the gap brackets in both lanes turn into coral brackets of exactly the same width, and the Decode row becomes 'Decode identical → TPOT unchanged'. The brackets carry no text of their own; their colours tie them to the rows.

beats.say: Caching is often said to make the model faster. It makes it start sooner, then stream at the same speed.
beats.show: On 'make the model faster', the lanes dim to 30% and, centre, white, 'makes the model faster' appears and is struck through in grey. On 'start sooner', teal 'makes it start sooner' appears beneath. On 'the same speed', the phrases fade, the lanes brighten, and the warm lane's pills slide right until its first pill sits directly under the cold lane's first pill; every following pill lines up exactly, gap for gap. Hold.

scenes.name: two levers, and why the phases split
scenes.visual: Keep x < 420, y < 110 clear. Split screen across the upper two thirds. Left half, amber outline: a panel titled 'Improving TTFT' with a lever icon, one line 'compute: keep the arithmetic units fed', above a grid of small amber arithmetic-unit squares fed by a blue prompt block. Right half, coral outline: 'Improving TPOT' with a lever icon, one line 'bandwidth: move fewer bytes per token', above a coral pipe carrying byte particles. Each panel's line shows while it is spoken and then shrinks away, leaving the title. A gauge sits under each title and persists: amber, reading '0.29 s', with a grey sub-label '2,000-token prompt' and, from b1 until 'Faster memory' in b2, a grey 26 px derivation '290 trillion ops ÷ 989 trillion/s'; coral, reading '42 ms'. Lower third, y 780 to 1000: one shared strip reused per beat, a chip card in b2 and three streaming lanes in b3. In b4 the two panels themselves pull apart and become two groups of machines. The idea: two waits with two different bottlenecks, so one change can move one gauge and leave the other alone, or even push it the wrong way, until the two phases get separate hardware.

beats.say: Different bottlenecks, different engineering. With a long prompt to read in, time to first token is a compute problem: keep the arithmetic units fed.
beats.show: On 'Different bottlenecks', the two panels slide in from the left and right edges, titles only, and both gauges light. On 'a long prompt', a long blue prompt block flows into the left panel's grid and every amber square lights. On 'compute problem', the line 'compute: keep the arithmetic units fed' lands under the left title; on 'fed', a few squares flicker dark and are refilled at once by incoming work particles.

beats.say: Time per output token is a bandwidth problem: move fewer bytes per token. Faster memory shrinks the gaps, and barely moves the pause.
beats.show: The left line shrinks away. On 'bandwidth problem', the right line 'bandwidth: move fewer bytes per token' lands and byte particles flow along the coral pipe; on 'fewer bytes', the particles shrink to half size. On 'Faster memory', the right line and the derivation shrink away and a chip card slides into the lower strip: 'H100', with '989 trillion ops/s' and '3.35 TB/s'; it flips to 'H200': the first line stays the same and dims, the second counts up to '4.8 TB/s' and glows coral. On 'shrinks the gaps', the coral gauge swings from '42 ms' to '29 ms' with a teal tick. On 'barely moves the pause', the amber gauge holds at '0.29 s' and a grey note appears beside it: 'same arithmetic'.

beats.say: A change can even hurt the other. Run each new prompt's prefill the moment it arrives, for a quicker first word, and every answer already streaming stalls.
beats.show: The chip card and the 'same arithmetic' note leave, and the coral gauge resets to '42 ms', the H100 again. The lower strip becomes three thin lanes, each led by a small user icon, with blue pills landing every 42 ms. On 'new prompt', a fourth user icon appears at the right with a long blue prompt block; on 'the moment it arrives', an amber block 'prefill ≈ 0.29 s' drops down across all three lanes. On 'stalls', every lane's pills stop at the block; when it ends, one more 42 ms step runs and the next pill lands, and the top lane's gap is bracketed '≈ 335 ms, 8× the usual gap'. The coral gauge kicks to '335 ms' and falls back to '42 ms' as the pills resume their rhythm.

beats.say: That is why serving systems eventually split the two phases onto different hardware.
beats.show: The lanes clear. On 'serving systems', the two panels pull apart toward the left and right edges. On 'split the two phases', each morphs into a group of server-rack icons, amber 'prefill machines' on the left and coral 'decode machines' on the right, each still carrying its gauge. On 'different hardware', a teal block labelled 'keys and values' travels along an arrow between the groups, tagged 'KV transfer', and a small grey inset of the six-stop route from earlier flashes with its 'KV transfer' stop highlighted, then fades.

scenes.name: throughput against goodput
scenes.visual: Keep x < 420, y < 110 clear. Far left, at mid-height, a G P U package icon emits blue token particles along a pipe running right. Top band: a long blue bar labelled 'Throughput · all tokens per second' with a counter at its right end. Below it, a dashed grey outline of the same length labelled 'Goodput · only the ones in time', which fills teal only with tokens that arrive in time. On the pipe at centre-left, a gate drawn as a narrow doorway with a stopwatch icon above it: tokens that pass in time turn teal and rise into the goodput bar; late ones turn grey and drop into a bin below the gate labelled 'missed target'. Top-right from b1: a one-line targets card, 'first token ≤ 1 s · next ≤ 50 ms', with a grey 'illustrative' tag. Bottom band from b2: a crowd of small user icons, each with a little screen. The idea: goodput is not a second machine, it is a filter on the first one's output.

beats.say: Operators count tokens. Throughput is every token generated per second. Goodput filters it down to tokens delivered inside the promised latency targets.
beats.show: On 'Operators count tokens', the G P U appears and blue particles stream along the pipe. On 'Throughput', the blue bar draws on with its label and its counter starts running. On 'Goodput filters it', the dashed outline draws on beneath with its label and the gate drops onto the pipe; most particles pass, turn teal and fill the goodput bar, a few turn grey and fall into the 'missed target' bin. On 'promised latency targets', the targets card slides in top-right with its 'illustrative' tag, and the gate's stopwatch shows the same two marks.

beats.say: Pack thousands of requests into huge, slow batches, and the counter looks impressive. But if every user stares at a blank screen for forty seconds, every token missed its target. Goodput is zero.
beats.show: On 'Pack thousands of requests', the crowd fills the bottom band and request pills from all of them pile into one enormous tray at the G P U. On 'the counter looks impressive', the stream thickens into a torrent and the throughput counter races upward, the blue bar glowing. On 'blank screen', every little screen in the crowd stays blank with a blinking cursor while a large stopwatch over the crowd runs to '40 s'; as it passes '1 s', the first-token mark on the targets card turns grey, and from then on every particle reaching the gate turns grey and drops into the bin. On 'Goodput is zero', the goodput bar drains to empty and its counter reads '0', while the throughput counter still races.

beats.say: Tokens nobody was willing to wait for. Goodput is throughput times the share that arrived in time.
beats.show: On 'nobody was willing to wait for', the camera pushes gently in on the overflowing grey bin, with the glowing throughput bar and the empty goodput outline side by side above it. On 'Goodput is throughput times', the camera eases back, the crowd, stopwatch, torrent and targets card clear, and an equation builds under the bars term by term: '1,000 tokens/s' as the throughput counter settles there; '× 70% in time' on 'the share'; '= 700 tokens/s' on 'arrived in time', as the goodput bar fills teal to 70% of its outline. A grey 'illustrative' tag sits beside the equation, and 300 grey tokens stack in the bin.

beats.say: Goodput, not raw throughput, is what production optimises. For anyone who operates a system rather than benchmarks one, no distinction matters more.
beats.show: The equation fades. On 'Goodput, not raw throughput', the word 'Goodput' enlarges and moves to centre in teal while 'Throughput' shrinks to grey above it. On 'operates a system', a small user-crowd icon appears beside 'Goodput'; on 'benchmarks one', a stopwatch-on-a-test-bench icon appears beside 'Throughput', greyed. Hold.

checks.claim: Van illustration (illustrative numbers, not from the atlas): 7,000 letters a week = 1,000 a day; the courier's 20 a day is a stated illustration
One request alone on an H100: 3.35 TB/s / 140 GB = 23.9, '≈ 24 tokens/s'; ten requests sharing one read: 3.35 TB/s / 14 GB = 239, '≈ 240 tokens/s' (weights only, matches ch12)
TPOT for one request: 140 GB / 3.35 TB/s = 41.8 ms on an H100, '≈ 42 ms'; 140 GB / 4.8 TB/s = 29.2 ms on an H200, '29 ms'

TTFT gauge for a 2,000-token prompt: about 290 trillion ops (ch12) at the H100's 989 trillion ops/s = 0.29 s at full speed; consistent with the atlas's 'half a second for a short prompt' once real chips run below peak

Ridge on the H100 = 989 / 3.35 = 295 ops per byte (the dashed ridge on the small roofline); a prefill longer than about 295 tokens is compute bound, hence 'with a long prompt to read in'. A 5-token warm prefill is 5 ops per byte, far below the ridge, so it waits on bytes

Example A, per CHAPTER_NOTES: 1,027 of 1,032 tokens held warm (a 99.5% hit), 5 prefilled; cold prefills all 1,032, 1,032 / 5 = 206 times the work. CORRECTION kept from ch15/ch16: atlas figs 44 and 47 say '906 of 911'; the film uses 1,027 of 1,032 so warm and cold describe the same conversation

Cold prefill of the 1,032-token weather conversation: 1,032 x 140 billion = 144.48 trillion ops plus 1.40 trillion of causal attention = 145.9 trillion; at 989 trillion ops/s = 147.5 ms, '≈ 148 ms' on screen (not narrated)

Warm prefill of 5 tokens: 0.7 trillion ops = 0.7 ms of arithmetic (the hairline amber sliver), but one read of 140 GB of weights = 41.8 ms plus 1,032 x 327,680 bytes of cache = 0.1 ms; total 41.9 ms, '≈ 42 ms: one 140 GB read'

206 times less prefill work gives only 3.5 times less waiting (147.5 ms / 41.9 ms), said 'three and a half times'. CORRECTION (reviewer): the first word comes 105.6 ms sooner, which rounds to '≈ 106 ms', not the earlier draft's truncated '≈ 105 ms'; it also matches the screen's own 148 - 42
Decode step after prefill, warm or cold: the cache is the same 1,032 tokens = 0.338 GB, so each step reads 140.34 GB, 41.9 ms on an H100, '≈ 42 ms' in both lanes

H100 to H200 swap: TPOT 41.8 to 29.2 ms; TTFT for the 2,000-token prompt stays 0.29 s because the H200's dense 16-bit arithmetic equals the H100's 989 trillion ops/s (same compute die; a hardware fact not stated in the atlas), and the prompt's ~146 GB of bytes take only 43.6 ms on an H100 and 30.4 ms on an H200, far inside the 293 ms of arithmetic ('barely moves', 'same arithmetic')

Interference (on screen, not narrated): the other streams' next token waits for the 293 ms prefill plus its own 41.8 ms decode step = 335 ms, 8.0 times the usual 41.8 ms gap, '≈ 335 ms, 8× the usual gap'. CORRECTION kept from the earlier draft: comparing the prefill alone (7.0 times) leaves out the step that actually makes the token
Goodput illustration (illustrative numbers, tagged on screen): 1,000 tokens/s x 70% in time = 700 tokens/s; 300 late

Storyboard scale for the cache-hit lanes at 3 px per ms: cold block 147.5 ms = 442 px, warm block and token spacing 41.9 ms = 126 px, axis 0 to 500 ms = 1,500 px; the cold lane's ninth token lands at 483 ms, inside the axis
